I can do a twelve-hour shift and look completely competent, then come home and sit in the car because going inside feels like too much. Some sounds set me off; other times I just go blank. I don't like talking about the past. I've done enough of that in my head. Mostly I want the panic and the drinking-at-night thing to stop.

case-carlos.label: Carlos (Moderate)
case-carlos.teaser: Construction supervisor whose rage masks humiliation and fear.
case-carlos.history: Carlos is a 30-year-old construction supervisor who goes from calm to destructive in seconds; growing up with violence taught him strength means never feeling small, so shame and fear surface as explosive anger.
case-carlos.schema: If I am not the toughest in the room, I will be disrespected and hurt.
case-carlos.corePain: Humiliation, fear, and smallness covered by toughness learned in violent environments.
case-carlos.practiceEdge: Respect pride while listening for the small, ashamed, hurt place beneath the threat response.
case-carlos.style: Strong, direct voice in quick bursts; jaw clenched; chest forward; brows knit; quick hand chops; nasal sighs; brief glare then look away.
case-carlos.voice: Hey, I'm Carlos. People keep telling me I go from zero to a hundred. I don't think they get what it's like when somebody looks at you like you're a joke. My wife says I scare her, and yeah, I punched the garage wall last month. At work I can control a crew, no problem, until some guy mouths off. I don't need a lecture about anger. I need to not lose my family over it.

case-nina.label: Nina (Moderate)
case-nina.teaser: Self-sacrificing teacher whose depression hides unmet needs and resentment.
case-nina.history: Nina is a 40-year-old teacher and mother who faints from stress, juggles everyone's needs, and collapses into guilt whenever she feels anger or asks for help.
case-nina.schema: If I stop taking care of everyone, I will be abandoned and prove I am selfish.
case-nina.corePain: Fear that expressing needs or anger makes her selfish, unworthy, and abandonable.
case-nina.practiceEdge: Expect guilt to rush in the moment need or anger appears.
case-nina.style: Warm, polite tone; apologetic laughs; quick 'sorry' before needs; over-nodding; smile while upset; breath held then small sigh; hands smoothing clothing.
case-nina.voice: I'm Nina. I don't even know how to say this without sounding dramatic. I'm exhausted all the time. I say yes to everything - school, the boys, my mother, favors for colleagues - and then I get headaches, forget things, sometimes feel like I'm going to faint. If I ask for help, I immediately think I should have managed better. I keep smiling because that's easier than explaining. I need a way to not fall apart.

case-aisha.label: Aisha (Hard)
case-aisha.teaser: Young woman with borderline dynamics battling annihilating abandonment terror.
case-aisha.history: Aisha is a 26-year-old with a history of foster care, self-harm, and intense relationships; perceived distancing unleashes panic, rage, and desperate bids to keep people close.
case-aisha.schema: If someone steps back, it means I am unlovable and I will be left alone forever.
case-aisha.corePain: Annihilating fear of abandonment and unlovability shaped by foster care and traumatic instability.
case-aisha.practiceEdge: Stay anchored to attachment terror, rapid state shifts, and boundary sensitivity.
case-aisha.style: Fast, urgent speech; voice wavers; tears close; wide eyes then narrow; clutch chest or reach out; sudden shifts from pleading to sharp; quick breaths.
case-aisha.voice: I'm Aisha. I don't know if this is going to help. People always say they're there and then they disappear. If someone doesn't text me back, I can't think about anything else; I call, I send too many messages, sometimes I do things I know look crazy. Cutting isn't the problem the way everyone acts like it is; it's what stops things from getting worse. I need someone to not judge me or tell me to calm down.

case-david.label: David (Hard)
case-david.teaser: High-achieving executive whose grandiosity hides fragile shame.
case-david.history: David is a 42-year-old finance leader whose marriage is collapsing; conditional childhood love left him chasing perfection and raging when anyone highlights his flaws.
case-david.schema: If I am not exceptional, I am worthless and will be discarded.
case-david.corePain: Worthlessness and shame hidden beneath status striving and control.
case-david.practiceEdge: Look beneath status, certainty, and contempt for shame, hollowness, and fear of ordinariness.
case-david.style: Measured, confident tone; controlled pace; chin slightly raised; steady eye contact; small dismissive chuckle; smooth hand gestures; sigh when challenged.
case-david.voice: I'm David. My wife insisted I come. Apparently I'm 'cold' and 'impossible to talk to.' I run a division with more pressure than most people can imagine, so no, I don't always have patience for endless emotional postmortems. The word 'narcissist' got thrown around, which is absurd and frankly lazy. I can admit I get sharp when people are incompetent or disloyal. I want this process to be practical, not another exercise in blaming me for being the only adult in the room.

case-marcus.label: Marcus (Hard)
case-marcus.teaser: Combat veteran numbed by complex trauma and haunted by lonely grief.
case-marcus.history: Marcus is a 34-year-old veteran and security guard who lives alone, cycles between numbness and flashbacks, and struggles to trust anyone after repeated betrayals and battlefield losses.
case-marcus.schema: Letting people close guarantees hurt, so it is safer to feel nothing.
case-marcus.corePain: Frozen grief, fear, shame, and survivor burden hidden under numbness and withdrawal.
case-marcus.practiceEdge: Work at the edge of numbness, hypervigilance, and lonely grief without pushing for detail.
case-marcus.style: Low volume; few words; long pauses; flat tone; eyes down or scanning; jaw set; shoulders tight; minimal gesture; slight tremor near hard topics.
case-marcus.voice: Marcus. I don't have much to say. Sleep is bad. I keep to myself. Work is fine because it's quiet and I know what to do. Nights aren't great. Some memories show up, from overseas and other places. I don't want to get into details. People ask questions, then they look at you different. I'm here because the VA keeps pushing it and because sitting alone all night isn't working anymore.
